data.narrative:
DiamFab is a seed-stage semiconductor company that has raised €8.7M to date. Valuation is anchored to a peer universe of 11 companies (3 public, 8 private) in the Chips & Semiconductors sector, including recent Series A rounds at SambaNova Systems, Rebellions, and d-Matrix.

Two triangulation methods apply to DiamFab's valuation. The Stage-Progression method, applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement to the €8.7M raised proxy, implies a valuation of $22M. The Peer-Median method examines three same-sector, adjacent-stage comparables: SambaNova ($11.0B), Rebellions ($2.3B), and d-Matrix ($2.0B). The median across these three yields $2.3B, though the wide range ($2.0B–$11.0B) reflects heterogeneity in capital efficiency and growth trajectories within the cohort. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (median 18.4x across ALAB, NVDA, AMD) cannot be applied due to absence of disclosed revenue.

The triangulated range spans $18M (low) to $2.7B (high), with a median of $1.2B across both applicable methods. The extreme dispersion—nearly three orders of magnitude—reflects fundamental uncertainty at the seed stage regarding technical validation, market timing, and capital intensity to commercialization. The Stage-Progression floor ($22M) represents conservative progression assumptions; the Peer-Median ceiling ($2.3B) carries risk that DiamFab may not achieve peer-level traction. Resolution hinges on near-term technical milestones and customer validation.
